newsitem.title: USA: Judge fines NY firm for fake U.S. war medals.
newsitem.headline: Judge fines NY firm for fake U.S. war medals.

text.p: A federal judge fined a New York company the maximum penalty of $80,000 Tuesday for manufacturing and selling 300 fake Medals of Honour, the nation's highest military award.
Judge William Bassler said the company, HLI Lordship, "violated a sacred trust" since it was the official manufacturer of the medal for the U.S. government.

"The offence cannot be overstated," Bassler said. "So many veterans, alive and dead, fought so valiantly to win the Medal of Honour from a grateful nation and this corporation has tarnished the medal for a few dollars."
He also ordered the firm to pay the government $22,500 -- the amount illegally gained through the sale of 300 fake medals for $75 each.
HLI Lordship, a respected manufacturer of medals and insignias for more than 50 years and based in Hauppauge on Long Island, admitted its guilt in the one-count indictment.
The case was heard in Federal Court in Newark, New Jersey because the medals were sold to collectors in the state. The company admitted making 600 fake medals between 1989 and 1991.
The sons of the founder of the company, Wes and Ward McAllister, were responsible for manufacturing the fake medals and had been fired, according to a company attorney.
A third brother, Michael McAllister, was not involved and is still employed by the company, which has 123 employees and had $10 million in sales last year.
